Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this on. OptimaBank's security team is performing a SIG/CAIQ review next week and we need a short packet showing Redwood's vulnerability management cadence and concrete evidence for CVE remediation timelines. Specifically:

- A simple index that maps your scan cadence (internal, third-party, dependency) to SLAs for high/critical CVEs.
- One or two example CVE closure snapshots (timestamps, owner, ticket ids) for recent high-severity items.
- Confirmation how exceptions are handled when a vendor patch isn't available (compensating controls / mitigations).

Hi Jamie — thanks for the clear ask. We're attaching a concise packet that maps our cadence to remediation SLAs and includes two closure snapshots. High level summary below; full files attached in my next email.

Summary (short):
- Scan cadence: internal SCA + SAST weekly, host/image vulnerability scans nightly for active infra, third-party dependency SBOM scans every 72 hours for production images.
- SLAs: Critical/exploitable (0-day with verified exploit or public PoC) = 7 days to mitigation or compensating control + daily updates; High = 30 days; Medium = 90 days; Low = patch window. Emergency exceptions documented and escalated to security@redwood.com and the appropriate eng owner.
- Evidence: two closure snapshots included (one infrastructure CVE, one dependency CVE) showing ticket id, triage note, patch commit SHA, and final verification timestamp.

I'll follow up with a short annotated playbook showing our exception flow for vendor-unpatchable items. If Optima needs an SLA letter signed, loop in Ben (cc'd) for an attestation.

Attachments upcoming: VM_Evidence_Index.xlsx; CVE_2026-3145-closure-snapshot.pdf

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Jamie — attaching the packet Naomi promised. Highlights and quick navigation below.

Attachments in this email: VM_Evidence_Index.xlsx (index + mapping), SIG-VM-Playbook-Redwood-annotated.docx

Quick navigation (VM_Evidence_Index.xlsx):
- Tab A: cadence-to-sla mapping (nightly/weekly/72h) and corresponding response SLA windows.
- Tab B: sample tickets (two recent high-priority examples) with ticket IDs, owners, dates opened/closed, commit SHAs and verification timestamps.
- Tab C: exception log template + compensating control checklist (used when vendor patches are delayed).

Exception handling (short):
- When a vendor patch is unavailable, we document risk, deploy compensating controls (nginx WAF rule, network ACL, temporary container isolation) and open an expedited remediation RACI with daily status to the customer security contact until closure.
- Exception durations and mitigation effectiveness are logged in the exception template; those records are what we provide for audits.

If you want a one-page attestation letter for your SIG portal stating our standard SLA windows (no custom commitments), I can draft and send for Ben's sign-off.

Cheers,
Monica Patel

We reviewed OptimaBank's ask and are providing a signed attestation for the standard remediation SLAs included in VM_Evidence_Index.xlsx. Key points in the attestation:

- Redwood Inference vulnerability remediation windows (standard): Critical/exploitable = 7 days with daily updates; High = 30 days; Medium = 90 days.

- Exceptions: we document and remediate with compensating controls; longer remediation windows require documented exception approval and are entered into our exception register which we share on request.
